ai-fluency-for-educators.title: AI Fluency for educators · Claude Academy
ai-fluency-for-educators.description: Helps faculty, instructional designers, and education leaders apply the 4D AI Fluency framework to course design, learning materials, and teaching practice.
ai-fluency-for-educators.text: AI Fluency for educators · Claude Academy Claude Academy AI Fluency Products  Resources   Search Loading AI Fluency Products  Resources  Courses   Academy / Courses  Courses AI Fluency for educators Helps faculty, instructional designers, and education leaders apply the 4D AI Fluency framework to course design, learning materials, and teaching practice.  4 lessons  1.5 hr  1 quiz  Completion badge Start course  Sign in to save progress 4 lessons · 1 quiz AI Fluency for educators  What you’ll learn By the end of this course, you’ll be able to  Explain how the 4Ds of the AI Fluency Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, Diligence) apply to teaching practice  Build a reusable teaching context document that captures your pedagogical values, constraints, and student profile  Apply the 4Ds to identify essential course content, map the learning journey, and articulate measurable learning objectives  Create lecture slides, study guides, in-class exercises, and assessments through AI collaboration grounded in your established context  Use the Description-Discernment loop to evaluate and refine AI-generated materials against your students' needs  Practice Diligence by verifying accuracy, documenting AI's role, and maintaining academic integrity in AI-assisted course development At Anthropic, we believe that empowering people with AI, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Responsible AI development and engagement isn't something any single discipline or viewpoint can fully address. It demands collaborative approaches that span a wide range of technical, creative, business, scientific, and educational domains. That's why we partnered with educators who bring complementary expertise to create this course on AI collaboration for educators. This course empowers faculty, instructional designers, and educational leaders to apply the 4D Framework to their own educational practice. Participants will learn to apply the 4D Framework to their own teaching practice, using AI as a thinking partner to enhance course design, create coherent learning materials, and develop authentic assessments while modeling responsible AI collaboration for their students. This course is the result of a long partnership between Anthropic and professors Rick Dakan from Ringling College of Art and Design and Joseph Feller from University College Cork. It builds on their experiences in training fellow educators and teaching the AI Fluency Framework to their students, and on feedback and questions that arose from our earlier course: AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations This course answers the question: how can I apply this framework to my personal teaching practice? The work was supported in part by the Higher Education Authority (Ireland) through the National Forum for the Enhancement of Teaching and Learning. Recommended prerequisites This course lightly covers the foundational AI Fluency concepts. However, for deeper understanding, participants should complete AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations before beginning this educator-focused curriculum. It is also recommended that learners have active teaching or curriculum development responsibilities as well as access to an AI chat tool for hands-on practice. Examples in this course will use Claude.ai, but any chatbot will work. About this course About this course (opens in new tab) Meet your instructors (opens in new tab) How we used AI in building the course (opens in new tab) Completion badge After finishing the course, you will have the opportunity to take a final assessment and earn a completion badge. Inside the course Introduction and AI Fluency Framework 2 lessons A summary of Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence applied to student contexts AI Fluency applications for educators 2 lessons Applying the 4D framework to course design and learning materials. class="mdx-article flex flex-col gap-md"><!--$--><p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">At Anthropic, we believe that empowering people with AI, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Responsible AI development and engagement isn't something any single discipline or viewpoint can fully address. It demands collaborative approaches that span a wide range of technical, creative, business, scientific, and educational domains. That's why we partnered with educators who bring complementary expertise to create this course on AI collaboration for educators.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course empowers faculty, instructional designers, and educational leaders to apply the 4D Framework to their own educational practice. Participants will learn to apply the 4D Framework to their own teaching practice, using AI as a thinking partner to enhance course design, create coherent learning materials, and develop authentic assessments while modeling responsible AI collaboration for their students.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course is the result of a long partnership between Anthropic and professors Rick Dakan from Ringling College of Art and Design and Joseph Feller from University College Cork. It builds on their experiences in training fellow educators and teaching the AI Fluency Framework to their students, and on feedback and questions that arose from our earlier course: AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations This course answers the question: how can I apply this framework to my personal teaching practice?</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The work was supported in part by the Higher Education Authority (Ireland) through the National Forum for the Enhancement of Teaching and Learning.</p>
<h2 id="recommended-prerequisites" class="mt-12 font-heading text-[1.375rem] font-medium tracking-tight first:mt-0 scroll-mt-[calc(var(--academy-header-h,3.5rem)+1.5rem)]">Recommended prerequisites</h2>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course lightly covers the foundational AI Fluency concepts. However, for deeper understanding, participants should complete AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations before beginning this educator-focused curriculum.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">It is also recommended that learners have active teaching or curriculum development responsibilities as well as access to an AI chat tool for hands-on practice. Examples in this course will use Claude.ai, but any chatbot will work.</p>

ai-fluency-for-k-12-educators.title: AI Fluency for pK–12 Educators · Claude Academy
ai-fluency-for-k-12-educators.description: Helps pK-12 educators build practical AI fluency through the 4D Framework, supporting student learning while staying true to their mission and values. Created in partnership with Teach For America.
ai-fluency-for-k-12-educators.text: AI Fluency for pK–12 Educators · Claude Academy Claude Academy AI Fluency Products  Resources   Search Loading AI Fluency Products  Resources  Courses   Academy / Courses  Courses AI Fluency for pK–12 Educators Helps pK-12 educators build practical AI fluency through the 4D Framework, supporting student learning while staying true to their mission and values. Created in partnership with Teach For America.  10 lessons  3 hr  1 quiz  Completion badge Start course  Sign in to save progress 10 lessons · 1 quiz AI Fluency for pK–12 Educators  What you’ll learn By the end of this course, you’ll be able to  Define AI Fluency and explain how the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, Diligence) applies to your teaching practice  Build a reusable context document that captures your role, students, and goals for future AI collaborations  Recognize the capabilities and limitations of generative AI, including hallucinations and knowledge cutoffs  Use the Description-Discernment loop to create and evaluate differentiated instructional materials  Apply the Delegation-Diligence loop to protect student data and navigate ethical gray areas in your practice  Draft personal ethical commitments and an AI value document grounded in your own values  Run a complete end-to-end 4D workflow on a real task from your own work This course is the result of a partnership between Anthropic and Teach For America, drawing on research with pK–12 educators about their actual needs, concerns, and aspirations for AI adoption. We believe that empowering people with skills to wield AI responsibly, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Educators are uniquely positioned to leverage AI for social good. This course helps pK–12 educators and staff build practical AI collaboration skills through the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence) in a human-centered way. In this course, we'll explore how the framework applies to common tasks in education. This course builds on Anthropic’s AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations course, adapted specifically for the pK–12 educator context where limited resources, multiple stakeholder accountabilities, and mission-driven work create unique considerations for AI collaboration. It also builds on the course Teach For America has produced for its constituents since 2023, as well as their ongoing practice since 2022 working to build AI fluency with and for educators across the United States. Recommended prerequisites This course lightly covers the foundational AI Fluency concepts. However, for deeper understanding, participants may wish to complete AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations and AI Capabilities and Limitations before beginning this educator-focused curriculum. It is also recommended that learners have access to an AI tool for hands-on practice. Examples in this course will use Claude.ai (opens in new tab) , but any AI tool will work. About the partners This course was created in partnership between Anthropic and Teach For America. Anthropic is a frontier AI safety company and the maker of Claude. Teach For America is a leadership development organization for those who want to co-create a more just world alongside young people in their communities. Today they are a network of more than 72,000 leaders who started in the classroom and remain in lifelong pursuit of the vision that one day, all children will have the opportunity to attain an excellent education. AI diligence statement In the development of this course, we engaged in extensive collaboration with Claude from Anthropic. The base content for this course came from: The AI Fluency Framework Practical Summary Document by Rick Dakan (at Ringling College of Art and Design) and Joseph Feller (at University College Cork) and related working documents and research notes. Technical and practical content provided by Anthropic. Knowledge about AI in pK–12 education came from Teach For America, drawing on the course they have produced for their constituents since 2023 and their ongoing work since 2022 building AI fluency with and for educators across the United States. Throughout this process, Claude assisted one or more of the human authors with structural development, resource and exercise design, and content drafting, critiquing, editing and rewriting. The human authors wrote, designed, edited and provided continual vision, expertise, critical judgment, and domain knowledge and made all final decisions about both content and approach. All AI-generated and co-created content underwent thorough validation, editing, and curation by the human authors. The final materials accurately reflect the human authors' understanding, expertise, and intended pedagogical approach. While AI assistance was instrumental in producing these materials, the human authors maintain responsibility for the content. This disclosure is made in the spirit of transparency advocated by the AI Fluency Framework and to acknowledge the evolving role of AI in educational content development and other creative and intellectual work. Inside the course Introduction and AI Fluency framework 3 lessons Define AI Fluency and learn the four interconnected competencies—Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence—that ground every productive AI collaboration as an educator. You'll articulate your values, goals, and constraints so every future AI interaction starts from the right context. How AI works 1 lesson Build a working mental model of what today's AI can and can't do reliably, and explore hands-on with an interactive next-token simulator so you understand why those limits matter for how you put it to work in teaching practice. Using AI responsibly 3 lessons Apply the Description-Discernment loop to creating high quality outputs and the Delegation-Diligence loop to working ethically with AI—practicing context-rich prompting, critical evaluation, and responsible data handling on the kinds of tasks you face every day. Putting it all together 1 lesson Bring all four dimensions of the 4D Framework together and apply it to a real task from your own work—then plan your next steps and earn your completion badge. leading-relaxed text-secondary"><em>This course is the result of a partnership between Anthropic and Teach For America, drawing on research with pK–12 educators about their actual needs, concerns, and aspirations for AI adoption.</em></p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">We believe that empowering people with skills to wield AI responsibly, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Educators are uniquely positioned to leverage AI for social good.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course helps pK–12 educators and staff build practical AI collaboration skills through the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence) in a human-centered way. In this course, we'll explore how the framework applies to common tasks in education.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course builds on Anthropic’s <em>AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations</em> course, adapted specifically for the pK–12 educator context where limited resources, multiple stakeholder accountabilities, and mission-driven work create unique considerations for AI collaboration. It also builds on the course Teach For America has produced for its constituents since 2023, as well as their ongoing practice since 2022 working to build AI fluency with and for educators across the United States.</p>
<h2 id="recommended-prerequisites" class="mt-12 font-heading text-[1.375rem] font-medium tracking-tight first:mt-0 scroll-mt-[calc(var(--academy-header-h,3.5rem)+1.5rem)]">Recommended prerequisites</h2>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course lightly covers the foundational AI Fluency concepts. However, for deeper understanding, participants may wish to complete <em>AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations</em> and <em>AI Capabilities and Limitations</em> before beginning this educator-focused curriculum.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">It is also recommended that learners have access to an AI tool for hands-on practice. Examples in this course will use <a data-cds="TextLink" aria-describedby="_R_13cjmicq_" href="http://claude.ai" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="cds-reset cds-text-link cds-text-link-underline inline cursor-pointer text-primary">Claude.ai<span id="_R_13cjmicq_" hidden="" class="sr-only">(opens in new tab)</span></a>, but any AI tool will work.</p>
<h2 id="about-the-partners" class="mt-12 font-heading text-[1.375rem] font-medium tracking-tight first:mt-0 scroll-mt-[calc(var(--academy-header-h,3.5rem)+1.5rem)]">About the partners</h2>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course was created in partnership between Anthropic and Teach For America. Anthropic is a frontier AI safety company and the maker of Claude. Teach For America is a leadership development organization for those who want to co-create a more just world alongside young people in their communities. Today they are a network of more than 72,000 leaders who started in the classroom and remain in lifelong pursuit of the vision that one day, all children will have the opportunity to attain an excellent education.</p>
<div class="my-lg flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-lg gap-y-md"><img src="/assets/v1/2cde17cb4146-m3tsu3hx.png" alt="Teach For America" loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="h-8 w-auto"/></div>
<h2 id="ai-diligence-statement" class="mt-12 font-heading text-[1.375rem] font-medium tracking-tight first:mt-0 scroll-mt-[calc(var(--academy-header-h,3.5rem)+1.5rem)]">AI diligence statement</h2>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">In the development of this course, we engaged in extensive collaboration with Claude from Anthropic.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The base content for this course came from:</p>
<ul class="flex list-disc flex-col gap-xs pl-lg">
<li class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The AI Fluency Framework Practical Summary Document by Rick Dakan (at Ringling College of Art and Design) and Joseph Feller (at University College Cork) and related working documents and research notes.</li>
<li class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">Technical and practical content provided by Anthropic. Knowledge about AI in pK–12 education came from Teach For America, drawing on the course they have produced for their constituents since 2023 and their ongoing work since 2022 building AI fluency with and for educators across the United States.</li>
</ul>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">Throughout this process, Claude assisted one or more of the human authors with structural development, resource and exercise design, and content drafting, critiquing, editing and rewriting. The human authors wrote, designed, edited and provided continual vision, expertise, critical judgment, and domain knowledge and made all final decisions about both content and approach.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">All AI-generated and co-created content underwent thorough validation, editing, and curation by the human authors. The final materials accurately reflect the human authors' understanding, expertise, and intended pedagogical approach. While AI assistance was instrumental in producing these materials, the human authors maintain responsibility for the content.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This disclosure is made in the spirit of transparency advocated by the AI Fluency Framework and to acknowledge the evolving role of AI in educational content development and other creative and intellectual work.</p><!--/$--></article><section class="flex flex-col gap-8"><h2 class="m-0 font-heading text-title font-medium tracking-tight">Inside the course</h2><div class="flex flex-col gap-3"><div class="flex items-baseline justify-between gap-md"><h3 class="m-0 font-heading text-heading font-medium text-primary [font-feature-settings:'ss01'_on]">Introduction and AI Fluency framework</h3><span class="shrink-0 text-footnote text-muted">3<!-- --> <!-- -->lessons</span></div><p class="m-0 text-body text-secondary">Define AI Fluency and learn the four interconnected competencies—Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence—that ground every productive AI collaboration as an educator. ai-fluency-for-nonprofits.title: AI Fluency for nonprofits · Claude Academy
ai-fluency-for-nonprofits.description: Build practical AI collaboration skills for nonprofit work using the 4D Framework: Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence. Covers research, writing, data analysis, and organization-wide AI adoption while staying true to your mission and values.
ai-fluency-for-nonprofits.text: AI Fluency for nonprofits · Claude Academy Claude Academy AI Fluency Products  Resources   Search Loading AI Fluency Products  Resources  Courses   Academy / Courses  Courses AI Fluency for nonprofits Build practical AI collaboration skills for nonprofit work using the 4D Framework: Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence. Covers research, writing, data analysis, and organization-wide AI adoption while staying true to your mission and values.  9 lessons  4 hr  1 quiz  Completion badge Start course  Sign in to save progress 9 lessons · 1 quiz AI Fluency for nonprofits  What you’ll learn By the end of this course, you’ll be able to  Define AI Fluency and explain how the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, Diligence) applies to nonprofit work  Apply the Description-Discernment loop to research policy landscapes, funding opportunities, and grant prospects relevant to your mission  Use Description and Discernment to draft and refine grant proposals and communications that reflect your organization's authentic voice  Evaluate AI tools' data handling policies and practice data hygiene to protect sensitive and personally identifiable information  Validate AI-assisted data analysis by testing against data you already understand before applying it to new questions  Combine all four competencies to design a repeatable AI-assisted workflow with appropriate human review  Draft an organizational AI policy that keeps humans in the loop and aligns AI use with your mission and values At Anthropic, we believe that empowering people with AI, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Nonprofit professionals are uniquely positioned to leverage AI for social good—but only if they can approach it intentionally, with resilience and clear purpose. This course helps nonprofit staff—whether in fundraising, communications, program delivery, operations, or leadership—build practical AI collaboration skills through the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence). In this course, we’ll explore how the framework applies to common non-profit tasks, and consider what it means to implement AI across a nonprofit organization. This course is the result of a partnership between Anthropic and GivingTuesday, drawing on research with nonprofit professionals about their actual needs, concerns, and aspirations for AI adoption. The work builds on our AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations course, adapted specifically for the nonprofit context where limited resources, multiple stakeholder accountabilities, and mission-driven work create unique considerations for AI collaboration. Recommended prerequisites This course lightly covers the foundational AI Fluency concepts. However, for deeper understanding, participants should complete AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations before beginning this nonprofit-focused curriculum. It is also recommended that learners have access to an AI chat tool for hands-on practice. Examples in this course will use Claude.ai (opens in new tab) , but any chatbot will work. Inside the course Introduction and AI Fluency framework 2 lessons Define AI Fluency and learn the four interconnected competencies—Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence—that form the foundation of this course. The Description-Discernment loop 2 lessons Practice crafting context-rich prompts and critically evaluating AI outputs through research and writing examples. The Delegation-Diligence loop 2 lessons Make thoughtful decisions about what tasks to delegate to AI while taking responsibility for high-stakes considerations like data privacy and analytical accuracy. Putting it all together 2 lessons Apply all four dimensions of the 4D Framework to automate workflows and integrate AI thoughtfully into your organization. flex-col gap-md"><!--$--><p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">At Anthropic, we believe that empowering people with AI, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Nonprofit professionals are uniquely positioned to leverage AI for social good—but only if they can approach it intentionally, with resilience and clear purpose.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course helps nonprofit staff—whether in fundraising, communications, program delivery, operations, or leadership—build practical AI collaboration skills through the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence). In this course, we’ll explore how the framework applies to common non-profit tasks, and consider what it means to implement AI across a nonprofit organization.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course is the result of a partnership between Anthropic and GivingTuesday, drawing on research with nonprofit professionals about their actual needs, concerns, and aspirations for AI adoption.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The work builds on our AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations course, adapted specifically for the nonprofit context where limited resources, multiple stakeholder accountabilities, and mission-driven work create unique considerations for AI collaboration.</p>

ai-fluency-for-pk-12-train-the-trainer.title: AI Fluency for pK-12 Train the Trainer · Claude Academy
ai-fluency-for-pk-12-train-the-trainer.description: This course empowers pK–12 educators to lead AI fluency training for their colleagues — equipping them with a ready-to-run workshop kit grounded in the 4D Framework, while staying true to educators' mission and values.
ai-fluency-for-pk-12-train-the-trainer.text: AI Fluency for pK-12 Train the Trainer · Claude Academy Claude Academy AI Fluency Products  Resources   Search Loading AI Fluency Products  Resources  Courses   Academy / Courses  Courses AI Fluency for pK-12 Train the Trainer This course empowers pK–12 educators to lead AI fluency training for their colleagues — equipping them with a ready-to-run workshop kit grounded in the 4D Framework, while staying true to educators' mission and values.  4 lessons  45 min Start course  Sign in to save progress 4 lessons AI Fluency for pK-12 Train the Trainer  What you’ll learn By the end of this course, you’ll be able to  See how this Train the Trainer kit connects to AI Fluency for pK-12 Educators  Understand why educator voice belongs at the center of AI decisions  Know what's in the kit and how to use it to run your own session This course is the result of a partnership between Anthropic and the American Federation of Teachers (AFT), built by educators, for educators. At Anthropic, we believe that empowering people with skills to wield AI responsibly, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Educators are uniquely positioned to leverage AI for social good—and to lead their colleagues in doing the same. This Train the Trainer course prepares pK–12 educators to facilitate AI fluency learning for other educators. It gives you everything you need to run your own workshop—the deck, the facilitator guide, and grade-band exercises—built around the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence). In this course, we'll explore how to bring the framework to a room full of teachers, from opening an honest conversation about AI to committing to a real task. The work builds on AI Fluency for pK–12 Educators , adapted into a train-the-trainer format so educators can lead this transition in their own schools and districts, on their own terms. Recommended prerequisites Before facilitating, we recommend completing AI Fluency for pK–12 Educators yourself, so you've built your own fluency with the 4D Framework before guiding others through it. For deeper foundational understanding, participants may also wish to complete AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations . It is also recommended that learners have access to an AI tool for hands-on practice. Examples in this course will use Claude.ai (opens in new tab) , but any AI tool will work. About the partners This course was created in partnership between Anthropic and the American Federation of Teachers (AFT), built by educators, for educators. Anthropic is a frontier AI safety company and the maker of Claude. The AFT is a union of professionals in education, healthcare, and public service. Inside the course Welcome 1 lesson From learner to trainer: what it means to facilitate AI fluency for your colleagues, and how this course prepares you to lead the workshop with confidence. pK-12 Train the Trainer Kit 3 lessons Everything you need to run the workshop: how to use the kit, the slide deck with its facilitator guide, and the learner workbook with grade-band exercises built around the 4D Framework. <p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">At Anthropic, we believe that empowering people with skills to wield AI responsibly, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Educators are uniquely positioned to leverage AI for social good—and to lead their colleagues in doing the same.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This Train the Trainer course prepares pK–12 educators to facilitate AI fluency learning for other educators. It gives you everything you need to run your own workshop—the deck, the facilitator guide, and grade-band exercises—built around the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence). In this course, we'll explore how to bring the framework to a room full of teachers, from opening an honest conversation about AI to committing to a real task.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The work builds on <em>AI Fluency for pK–12 Educators</em>, adapted into a train-the-trainer format so educators can lead this transition in their own schools and districts, on their own terms.</p>

For deeper foundational understanding, participants may also wish to complete <em>AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations</em>.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">It is also recommended that learners have access to an AI tool for hands-on practice. ai-fluency-for-small-businesses.title: AI Fluency for Small Businesses · Claude Academy
ai-fluency-for-small-businesses.description: Helps small business owners and staff build practical AI collaboration skills using the 4D Framework: Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence. Applies the framework to everyday business tasks like research, customer data, and operations while staying true to your mission and values.
ai-fluency-for-small-businesses.text: AI Fluency for Small Businesses · Claude Academy Claude Academy AI Fluency Products  Resources   Search Loading AI Fluency Products  Resources  Courses   Academy / Courses  Courses AI Fluency for Small Businesses Helps small business owners and staff build practical AI collaboration skills using the 4D Framework: Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence. Applies the framework to everyday business tasks like research, customer data, and operations while staying true to your mission and values.  9 lessons  4 hr  1 quiz  Completion badge Start course  Sign in to save progress 9 lessons · 1 quiz AI Fluency for Small Businesses  What you’ll learn By the end of this course, you’ll be able to  Define AI Fluency and the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, Diligence) and explain how each competency applies to small business work  Recognize the capabilities and limitations of generative AI, including hallucinations and knowledge cutoffs, to set realistic expectations for business use  Apply the Description-Discernment loop to craft effective prompts and critically evaluate AI-generated research before acting on it  Practice data hygiene and privacy safeguards when sharing sensitive business information with AI tools  Decide which repetitive business tasks are good candidates for AI automation and which should stay human-led  Build a repeatable AI-augmented workflow using Product, Process, and Performance Descriptions and plan for Diligence at every stage  Draft an AI use policy for your business that addresses transparency, accountability, and concerns about AI dependency  Apply the full 4D Framework to a real task from your own business operations At Anthropic, we believe that empowering people with AI, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Small businesses are uniquely positioned to leverage AI to advance their mission—but only if they can approach it intentionally, with resilience and clear purpose. This course helps small business staff—whether in customer interactions, back-office management, supply chain operations, or leadership—build practical AI collaboration skills through the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence). In this course, we’ll explore how the framework applies to common small business tasks, and consider what it means to implement AI across a small business. This course is the result of a partnership between Anthropic, PayPal, Prospect Butcher, and MAKS Enterprises TIPM Rebuilders, drawing on research with small business professionals about their actual needs, concerns, and aspirations for AI adoption. The work builds on our AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations course, adapted specifically for the small business context where limited resources, business accountabilities, and customer experience create unique considerations for AI collaboration. Recommended prerequisites This course lightly covers the foundational AI Fluency concepts. However, for deeper understanding, participants should complete AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations before beginning this small business-focused curriculum. It is also recommended that learners have access to an AI chat tool for hands-on practice. Examples in this course will use Claude.ai (opens in new tab) , but any chatbot will work. About the partners This course was created in partnership between Anthropic, PayPal, Prospect Butcher Company, and MAKS TIPM Rebuilders. Anthropic is a frontier AI safety company and the maker of Claude. PayPal is a platform that helps businesses of all sizes make selling and shopping simple and secure. Prospect Butcher Company and MAKS TIPM Rebuilders are the two small businesses featured throughout the course — a Brooklyn butcher shop and an automotive power-module rebuilder, each using AI to grow. AI diligence statement In the development of the AI Fluency: Framework and Foundations course, we engaged in extensive collaboration with Claude from Anthropic. The base content for this course came from: The AI Fluency Framework Practical Summary Document by Rick Dakan (at Ringling College of Art and Design) and Joseph Feller (at University College Cork) and related working documents and research notes. Technical/practical content provided by Kristen Swanson and Kyra Atekwana (Anthropic). Knowledge about AI in the small business setting came from Mak Cabessa (MAKS TIPM Rebuilders), Corey Hammond (Prospect Butcher Company), and Jordan Medina (PayPal). Throughout this process, Claude assisted one or more of the human authors with structural development, resource and exercise design, and content drafting, critiquing, editing and rewriting. The human authors wrote, designed, edited and provided continual vision, expertise, critical judgment, and domain knowledge and made all final decisions about both content and approach. All AI-generated and co-created content underwent thorough validation, editing, and curation by the human authors. The final materials accurately reflect the human authors' understanding, expertise, and intended pedagogical approach. While AI assistance was instrumental in producing these materials, the human authors maintain responsibility for the content. This disclosure is made in the spirit of transparency advocated by the AI Fluency Framework and to acknowledge the evolving role of AI in educational content development and other creative and intellectual work. Inside the course Introduction and AI Fluency framework 2 lessons Define AI Fluency and learn the four interconnected competencies—Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence—that ground every productive AI collaboration in your business. You'll articulate your values, goals, and constraints so every future AI interaction starts from the right context. How AI works 2 lessons Build a working mental model of what today's AI can and can't do reliably, and explore hands-on with an interactive next-token simulator so you understand why those limits matter for how you put it to work in your business. The Description-Discernment loop 1 lesson Apply the Description-Discernment loop to real research and the Delegation-Diligence loop to working with customer data—practicing context-rich prompting, critical evaluation, and responsible data handling on the kinds of tasks you face every day. The Delegation-Diligence loop 1 lesson Putting it all together 2 lessons Bring all four dimensions of the 4D Framework together to build a repeatable AI-augmented workflow and a short, honest AI use policy that fits your business and your team—then plan your next steps and earn your completion badge. class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">At Anthropic, we believe that empowering people with AI, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Small businesses are uniquely positioned to leverage AI to advance their mission—but only if they can approach it intentionally, with resilience and clear purpose.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course helps small business staff—whether in customer interactions, back-office management, supply chain operations, or leadership—build practical AI collaboration skills through the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence). In this course, we’ll explore how the framework applies to common small business tasks, and consider what it means to implement AI across a small business.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course is the result of a partnership between Anthropic, PayPal, Prospect Butcher, and MAKS Enterprises TIPM Rebuilders, drawing on research with small business professionals about their actual needs, concerns, and aspirations for AI adoption.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The work builds on our AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations course, adapted specifically for the small business context where limited resources, business accountabilities, and customer experience create unique considerations for AI collaboration.</p>
<h2 id="recommended-prerequisites" class="mt-12 font-heading text-[1.375rem] font-medium tracking-tight first:mt-0 scroll-mt-[calc(var(--academy-header-h,3.5rem)+1.5rem)]"><strong>Recommended prerequisites</strong></h2>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course lightly covers the foundational AI Fluency concepts. However, for deeper understanding, participants should complete <em>AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations</em> before beginning this small business-focused curriculum.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">It is also recommended that learners have access to an AI chat tool for hands-on practice. Examples in this course will use <a data-cds="TextLink" aria-describedby="_R_13cjmicq_" href="http://claude.ai" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="cds-reset cds-text-link cds-text-link-underline inline cursor-pointer text-primary">Claude.ai<span id="_R_13cjmicq_" hidden="" class="sr-only">(opens in new tab)</span></a>, but any chatbot will work.</p>
<h2 id="about-the-partners" class="mt-12 font-heading text-[1.375rem] font-medium tracking-tight first:mt-0 scroll-mt-[calc(var(--academy-header-h,3.5rem)+1.5rem)]">About the partners</h2>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course was created in partnership between Anthropic, PayPal, Prospect Butcher Company, and MAKS TIPM Rebuilders. Anthropic is a frontier AI safety company and the maker of Claude. PayPal is a platform that helps businesses of all sizes make selling and shopping simple and secure. Prospect Butcher Company and MAKS TIPM Rebuilders are the two small businesses featured throughout the course — a Brooklyn butcher shop and an automotive power-module rebuilder, each using AI to grow.</p>

<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">In the development of the AI Fluency: Framework and Foundations course, we engaged in extensive collaboration with Claude from Anthropic.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The base content for this course came from:</p>

<li class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The AI Fluency Framework Practical Summary Document by Rick Dakan (at Ringling College of Art and Design) and Joseph Feller (at University College Cork) and related working documents and research notes.</li>
<li class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">Technical/practical content provided by Kristen Swanson and Kyra Atekwana (Anthropic). Knowledge about AI in the small business setting came from Mak Cabessa (MAKS TIPM Rebuilders), Corey Hammond (Prospect Butcher Company), and Jordan Medina (PayPal).</li>
</ul>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">Throughout this process, Claude assisted one or more of the human authors with structural development, resource and exercise design, and content drafting, critiquing, editing and rewriting. The human authors wrote, designed, edited and provided continual vision, expertise, critical judgment, and domain knowledge and made all final decisions about both content and approach.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">All AI-generated and co-created content underwent thorough validation, editing, and curation by the human authors. The final materials accurately reflect the human authors' understanding, expertise, and intended pedagogical approach. While AI assistance was instrumental in producing these materials, the human authors maintain responsibility for the content.</p>

ai-fluency-for-students.title: AI Fluency for students · Claude Academy
ai-fluency-for-students.description: Helps students build AI fluency skills for learning, career planning, and academic success through responsible AI collaboration. Applies the 4D framework (delegation, description, discernment, diligence) to student life.
ai-fluency-for-students.text: AI Fluency for students · Claude Academy Claude Academy AI Fluency Products  Resources   Search Loading AI Fluency Products  Resources  Courses   Academy / Courses  Courses AI Fluency for students Helps students build AI fluency skills for learning, career planning, and academic success through responsible AI collaboration. Applies the 4D framework (delegation, description, discernment, diligence) to student life.  5 lessons  3 hr  1 quiz  Completion badge Start course  Sign in to save progress 5 lessons · 1 quiz AI Fluency for students  What you’ll learn By the end of this course, you’ll be able to  Explain what AI Fluency means and why it matters for your academic and professional future  Apply the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, Diligence) to your AI interactions as a student  Distinguish between using AI to do work for you and using AI to genuinely learn  Configure an AI learning partner and living learning journal that enhance rather than replace your learning  Use AI for career exploration, CV/resume improvement, and interview practice while maintaining your authentic voice  Create a personal AI collaboration policy and maintain your role as "the human in the loop" You've probably tried AI—maybe to help with an essay, solve a problem, or just explore what it can do. But there's a difference between using AI and being fluent with it. This course teaches students how to collaborate with AI effectively, efficiently, ethically, and safely across learning and career contexts. Rather than focusing on shortcuts or prompt tricks, this course develops lasting skills through the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence). Students learn to use AI as a thinking partner that enhances their learning and career development rather than replacing their own critical thinking and creativity. Through practical applications in academic work and career planning, students discover how to leverage AI to understand concepts more deeply, develop professional skills, and prepare for a future where AI Fluency is essential. The course emphasizes being 'the human in the loop'— maintaining agency, judgment, and responsibility while working thoughtfully with AI systems. This course is the result of a long partnership between Anthropic and professors Rick Dakan from Ringling College of Art and Design and Joseph Feller from University College Cork. It addresses the fundamental question students face: how can I use AI to genuinely enhance my learning and career success without compromising my own growth and integrity? The work was supported in part by the Higher Education Authority (Ireland) through the National Forum for the Enhancement of Teaching and Learning. Recommended prerequisites This course lightly covers the foundational AI Fluency concepts. However, for deeper understanding, participants should complete AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations before beginning this student-focused curriculum. It is also recommended that learners have access to an AI chat tool for hands-on practice. Examples in this course will use Claude.ai, but any chatbot will work. About this course About this course (opens in new tab) Meet your instructors (opens in new tab) How we used AI in building the course (opens in new tab) Completion badge After finishing the course, you will have the opportunity to take a final assessment and earn a completion badge. Inside the course Introduction and AI Fluency Framework 2 lessons A summary of Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence applied to student contexts AI Fluency Framework applications for students 2 lessons Applying the 4D framework to learning and career planning. Conclusion & badge 2 lessons Developing personal commitments for responsible AI collaboration and maintaining agency. gap-md"><!--$--><p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">You've probably tried AI—maybe to help with an essay, solve a problem, or just explore what it can do. But there's a difference between using AI and being fluent with it. This course teaches students how to collaborate with AI effectively, efficiently, ethically, and safely across learning and career contexts.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">Rather than focusing on shortcuts or prompt tricks, this course develops lasting skills through the 4D Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence). Students learn to use AI as a thinking partner that enhances their learning and career development rather than replacing their own critical thinking and creativity.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">Through practical applications in academic work and career planning, students discover how to leverage AI to understand concepts more deeply, develop professional skills, and prepare for a future where AI Fluency is essential. The course emphasizes being 'the human in the loop'— maintaining agency, judgment, and responsibility while working thoughtfully with AI systems.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course is the result of a long partnership between Anthropic and professors Rick Dakan from Ringling College of Art and Design and Joseph Feller from University College Cork. It addresses the fundamental question students face: how can I use AI to genuinely enhance my learning and career success without compromising my own growth and integrity?</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The work was supported in part by the Higher Education Authority (Ireland) through the National Forum for the Enhancement of Teaching and Learning.</p>
<h2 id="recommended-prerequisites" class="mt-12 font-heading text-[1.375rem] font-medium tracking-tight first:mt-0 scroll-mt-[calc(var(--academy-header-h,3.5rem)+1.5rem)]">Recommended prerequisites</h2>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course lightly covers the foundational AI Fluency concepts. However, for deeper understanding, participants should complete AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations before beginning this student-focused curriculum.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">It is also recommended that learners have access to an AI chat tool for hands-on practice. Examples in this course will use Claude.ai, but any chatbot will work.</p>

ai-fluency-framework-foundations.description: Learn to collaborate with AI effectively, efficiently, ethically, and safely using the 4D framework: Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence.
ai-fluency-framework-foundations.text: AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations · Claude Academy Claude Academy AI Fluency Products  Resources   Search Loading AI Fluency Products  Resources  Courses   Academy / Courses  Courses AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations Learn to collaborate with AI effectively, efficiently, ethically, and safely using the 4D framework: Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence.  14 lessons  4 hr  1 quiz  Completion badge Start course  Sign in to save progress 14 lessons · 1 quiz AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations  What you’ll learn By the end of this course, you’ll be able to  Explain what AI Fluency means and why it matters for collaborating with AI effectively, efficiently, ethically, and safely  Apply the 4D framework of Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence to your AI interactions  Distinguish Automation, Augmentation, and Agency as three ways of engaging with AI  Describe how generative AI and large language models work, including their key capabilities and limitations  Make strategic Delegation decisions using Problem Awareness, Platform Awareness, and Task Delegation  Communicate clearly with AI through Product, Process, and Performance Description and foundational prompting techniques  Evaluate AI outputs, processes, and behavior critically and refine results through the Description-Discernment loop  Practice Creation, Transparency, and Deployment Diligence to take responsibility for AI-assisted work At Anthropic, we believe that empowering people with AI, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Responsible AI development and engagement isn't something any single discipline or viewpoint can fully address. It demands collaborative approaches that span a wide range of technical, creative, business, scientific, and educational domains. That's why we partnered with educators who bring complementary expertise to create this foundational course on AI collaboration. This course is the result of a long partnership between Anthropic and professors Rick Dakan from Ringling College of Art and Design and Joseph Feller from University College Cork. Rick and Joe developed the AI Fluency Framework in 2023-2024, based on their research exploring how AI tools like Claude were transforming creative and business processes. When we saw the framework, we immediately recognized a shared vision: helping people interact with AI effectively and responsibly, beyond just “cool prompts.” Their framework offered exactly the kind of multidisciplinary perspective we believe is essential for navigating AI’s impact on society. The AI Fluency Framework they created — four interconnected competencies (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence) — enables more effective, efficient, ethical, and safe human-AI collaboration, regardless of which new AI models or tools emerge. We collaborated to develop this course based on their framework, bringing together our collective expertise in AI systems, education, creativity, and business innovation. The work was supported in part by the Higher Education Authority (Ireland) through the National Forum for the Enhancement of Teaching and Learning. This framework has already informed undergraduate and postgraduate courses at both Ringling College and University College Cork, as well as staff training initiatives and community outreach events. Now, we’re excited to share these insights more broadly through this open online course. Our goal is to make AI Fluency accessible and useful to everyone, no matter what stage of AI expertise you find yourself at. We hope you find it valuable in navigating the evolving landscape of AI collaboration. About this course About this course (opens in new tab) Meet your instructors (opens in new tab) How we used AI in building the course (opens in new tab) Completion badge After finishing the course, you will have the opportunity to take a final assessment and earn a completion badge. AI diligence statement In the development of the AI Fluency: Framework and Foundations course, we engaged in extensive collaboration with Claude 3.7 from Anthropic. The base content for this course came from: The AI Fluency Framework Practical Summary Document by Rick Dakan (at Ringling College of Art and Design) and Joseph Feller (at University College Cork) and related working documents and research notes Slide decks and lecture transcripts from multiple university courses, guest lectures, and research talks delivered by Feller and/or Dakan Technical/practical content provided by Maggie Vo and Drew Bent (Anthropic) Throughout this process, Claude assisted one or more of the human authors with structural development, resource and exercise design, and content drafting, critiquing, editing and rewriting. The human authors wrote, designed, edited and provided continual vision, expertise, critical judgment, and domain knowledge and made all final decisions about both content and approach. All AI-generated and co-created content underwent thorough validation, editing, and curation by the human authors. The final materials accurately reflect the human authors' understanding, expertise, and intended pedagogical approach. While AI assistance was instrumental in producing these materials, the human authors maintain responsibility for the content. This disclosure is made in the spirit of transparency advocated by the AI Fluency Framework and to acknowledge the evolving role of AI in educational content development and other creative and intellectual work. (Part 1) Generative AI fundamentals Capabilities & limitations Delegation A closer look at Delegation Project planning and Delegation Description A closer look at Description Deep Dive 2: Effective prompting techniques Effective prompting techniques Discernment A closer look at Discernment The Description-Discernment loop The Description-Discernment loop Diligence A closer look at Diligence Conclusion & badge Conclusion Course quiz  Quiz Additional activities Completion badge © 2026 Anthropic PBC Privacy choices Privacy policy Usage policy 

gap-md"><!--$--><p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">At Anthropic, we believe that empowering people with AI, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Responsible AI development and engagement isn't something any single discipline or viewpoint can fully address. It demands collaborative approaches that span a wide range of technical, creative, business, scientific, and educational domains. That's why we partnered with educators who bring complementary expertise to create this foundational course on AI collaboration.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course is the result of a long partnership between Anthropic and professors Rick Dakan from Ringling College of Art and Design and Joseph Feller from University College Cork. Rick and Joe developed the AI Fluency Framework in 2023-2024, based on their research exploring how AI tools like Claude were transforming creative and business processes. When we saw the framework, we immediately recognized a shared vision: helping people interact with AI effectively and responsibly, beyond just “cool prompts.” Their framework offered exactly the kind of multidisciplinary perspective we believe is essential for navigating AI’s impact on society.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The AI Fluency Framework they created — four interconnected competencies (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence) — enables more effective, efficient, ethical, and safe human-AI collaboration, regardless of which new AI models or tools emerge. We collaborated to develop this course based on their framework, bringing together our collective expertise in AI systems, education, creativity, and business innovation. The work was supported in part by the Higher Education Authority (Ireland) through the National Forum for the Enhancement of Teaching and Learning.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This framework has already informed undergraduate and postgraduate courses at both Ringling College and University College Cork, as well as staff training initiatives and community outreach events. Now, we’re excited to share these insights more broadly through this open online course.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">Our goal is to make AI Fluency accessible and useful to everyone, no matter what stage of AI expertise you find yourself at. We hope you find it valuable in navigating the evolving landscape of AI collaboration.</p>

<h2 id="ai-diligence-statement" class="mt-12 font-heading text-[1.375rem] font-medium tracking-tight first:mt-0 scroll-mt-[calc(var(--academy-header-h,3.5rem)+1.5rem)]">AI diligence statement</h2>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">In the development of the AI Fluency: Framework and Foundations course, we engaged in extensive collaboration with Claude 3.7 from Anthropic.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The base content for this course came from:</p>
<ul class="flex list-disc flex-col gap-xs pl-lg">
<li class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The AI Fluency Framework Practical Summary Document by Rick Dakan (at Ringling College of Art and Design) and Joseph Feller (at University College Cork) and related working documents and research notes</li>
<li class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">Slide decks and lecture transcripts from multiple university courses, guest lectures, and research talks delivered by Feller and/or Dakan</li>
<li class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">Technical/practical content provided by Maggie Vo and Drew Bent (Anthropic)</li>
</ul>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">Throughout this process, Claude assisted one or more of the human authors with structural development, resource and exercise design, and content drafting, critiquing, editing and rewriting. The human authors wrote, designed, edited and provided continual vision, expertise, critical judgment, and domain knowledge and made all final decisions about both content and approach.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">All AI-generated and co-created content underwent thorough validation, editing, and curation by the human authors. The final materials accurately reflect the human authors' understanding, expertise, and intended pedagogical approach. While AI assistance was instrumental in producing these materials, the human authors maintain responsibility for the content.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This disclosure is made in the spirit of transparency advocated by the AI Fluency Framework and to acknowledge the evolving role of AI in educational content development and other creative and intellectual work.</p><!--/$--></article></div><nav aria-label="Course outline" class="hidden w-72 shrink-0 self-start lg:flex lg:flex-col"><div class="flex flex-col gap-[18px]"><div class="flex flex-col gap-1"><span class="text-footnote text-muted px-2 pb-0.5 pt-2">Introduction to AI Fluency</span><ul class="flex flex-col gap-[2px]"><li><a href="/courses/ai-fluency-framework-foundations/introduction-to-ai-fluency" class="flex items-center gap-2.5 rounded text-body transition-colors duration-fast min-h-[30px] px-2 py-1 text-secondary hover:bg-fill-ghost-hover hover:text-primary"><span class="min-w-0 flex-1 text-pretty">Introduction to AI Fluency</span></a></li></ul></div><div class="flex flex-col gap-1"><span class="text-footnote text-muted px-2 pb-0.5 pt-2">The AI Fluency Framework</span><ul class="flex flex-col gap-[2px]"><li><a href="/courses/ai-fluency-framework-foundations/why-do-we-need-ai-fluency" class="flex items-center gap-2.5 rounded text-body transition-colors duration-fast min-h-[30px] px-2 py-1 text-secondary hover:bg-fill-ghost-hover hover:text-primary"><span class="min-w-0 flex-1 text-pretty">Why do we need AI Fluency?</span></a></li><li><a href="/courses/ai-fluency-framework-foundations/the-4d-framework" class="flex items-center gap-2.5 rounded text-body transition-colors duration-fast min-h-[30px] px-2 py-1 text-secondary hover:bg-fill-ghost-hover hover:text-primary"><span class="min-w-0 flex-1 text-pretty">The 4D Framework</span></a></li></ul></div><div class="flex flex-col gap-1"><span class="text-footnote text-muted px-2 pb-0.5 pt-2">Deep Dive 1: What is Generative AI? teaching-ai-fluency.title: Teaching AI Fluency · Claude Academy
teaching-ai-fluency.description: Equips academic faculty and instructional designers to teach and assess AI fluency in instructor-led settings. Builds on the 4D AI Fluency Framework with strategies for assessment, assignment design, and discipline-specific application.
teaching-ai-fluency.text: Teaching AI Fluency · Claude Academy Claude Academy AI Fluency Products  Resources   Search Loading AI Fluency Products  Resources  Courses   Academy / Courses  Courses Teaching AI Fluency Equips academic faculty and instructional designers to teach and assess AI fluency in instructor-led settings. Builds on the 4D AI Fluency Framework with strategies for assessment, assignment design, and discipline-specific application.  7 lessons  4.5 hr  1 quiz  Completion badge Start course  Sign in to save progress 7 lessons · 1 quiz Teaching AI Fluency  What you’ll learn By the end of this course, you’ll be able to  Select and adapt a linear, non-linear, focused, or loop-based approach to teaching the AI Fluency Framework for your students and context  Teach the Delegation-Diligence and Description-Discernment loops as connected strategic and tactical processes  Apply outcome, process, and reflection-based assessment strategies to evaluate the 4D competencies  Design authentic, iterative assignments that develop AI Fluency while keeping grading manageable  Analyze AI's impact on curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment in your discipline  Create discipline-specific applications of the 4Ds in collaboration with colleagues At Anthropic, we believe that empowering people with AI, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Responsible AI development and engagement isn't something any single discipline or viewpoint can fully address. It demands collaborative approaches that span a wide range of technical, creative, business, scientific, and educational domains. That's why we partnered with educators who bring complementary expertise to create this course on AI collaboration for educators. This course empowers faculty, instructional designers, and educational leaders to apply the 4D Framework to their own educational practice. Participants will learn to apply the 4D Framework to their own teaching practice, using AI as a thinking partner to enhance course design, create coherent learning materials, and develop authentic assessments while modeling responsible AI collaboration for their students. This course is the result of a long partnership between Anthropic and professors Rick Dakan from Ringling College of Art and Design and Joseph Feller from University College Cork. It builds on their experiences in training fellow educators and teaching the AI Fluency Framework to their students, and on feedback and questions that arose from our earlier course: AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations This course answers the question: how can I apply this framework to my personal teaching practice? The work was supported in part by the Higher Education Authority (Ireland) through the National Forum for the Enhancement of Teaching and Learning. Recommended prerequisites This course lightly covers the foundational AI Fluency concepts. However, for deeper understanding, participants should complete AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations before beginning this educator-focused curriculum. It is also recommended that learners have active teaching or curriculum development responsibilities as well as access to an AI chat tool for hands-on practice. Examples in this course will use Claude.ai, but any chatbot will work. About this course About this course (opens in new tab) Meet your instructors (opens in new tab) How we used AI in building the course (opens in new tab) Completion badge After finishing the course, you will have the opportunity to take a final assessment and earn a completion badge. Inside the course Introduction and approaches to teaching AI Fluency 3 lessons Scaffolding student AI Fluency through the 4D Framework. Assessing AI Fluency 2 lessons Designing assessments and assignments that develop and measure student AI Fluency alongside disciplinary expertise. AI's Impact on disciplinary content 2 lessons Building institutional capacity for responsible and meaningful AI integration in pedagogy, assessment, and curricula across disciplines. Introduction and approaches to teaching AI Fluency Welcome & approaches to teaching AI Fluency The Delegation-Diligence loop The Description-Discernment loop Assessing AI Fluency How do we assess the 4Ds? Designing assignments for AI Fluency AI's Impact on disciplinary content AI's impact and your discipline Applying discipline expertise to AI Fluency Conclusion & badge Course quiz  Quiz Completion badge © 2026 Anthropic PBC Privacy choices Privacy policy Usage policy 

class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">At Anthropic, we believe that empowering people with AI, and ensuring that AI makes safe contributions to society, requires engaging with a wide range of human perspectives and experiences. Responsible AI development and engagement isn't something any single discipline or viewpoint can fully address. It demands collaborative approaches that span a wide range of technical, creative, business, scientific, and educational domains. That's why we partnered with educators who bring complementary expertise to create this course on AI collaboration for educators.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course empowers faculty, instructional designers, and educational leaders to apply the 4D Framework to their own educational practice. Participants will learn to apply the 4D Framework to their own teaching practice, using AI as a thinking partner to enhance course design, create coherent learning materials, and develop authentic assessments while modeling responsible AI collaboration for their students.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course is the result of a long partnership between Anthropic and professors Rick Dakan from Ringling College of Art and Design and Joseph Feller from University College Cork. It builds on their experiences in training fellow educators and teaching the AI Fluency Framework to their students, and on feedback and questions that arose from our earlier course: AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations This course answers the question: how can I apply this framework to my personal teaching practice?</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">The work was supported in part by the Higher Education Authority (Ireland) through the National Forum for the Enhancement of Teaching and Learning.</p>
<h2 id="recommended-prerequisites" class="mt-12 font-heading text-[1.375rem] font-medium tracking-tight first:mt-0 scroll-mt-[calc(var(--academy-header-h,3.5rem)+1.5rem)]">Recommended prerequisites</h2>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">This course lightly covers the foundational AI Fluency concepts. However, for deeper understanding, participants should complete AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations before beginning this educator-focused curriculum.</p>
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-secondary">It is also recommended that learners have active teaching or curriculum development responsibilities as well as access to an AI chat tool for hands-on practice. Examples in this course will use Claude.ai, but any chatbot will work.</p>
